<section class="about-section" id="about"><div class="wrap"><h2>About us</h2><div class="about-copy"><p>We are a research group at the University of Granada working at the intersection of causal inference, biostatistics and computational epidemiology. We develop and study methods for estimating causal effects from observational data, including complex treatments, targeted learning and conformal inference. Our research addresses questions in population health, such as socioeconomic inequalities in cancer outcomes and the effects of emergency presentation on cancer survival. We also develop <a href="#software">open-source software</a> in R and Stata and share <a href="#resources">teaching materials</a> to make statistical and causal methods more accessible to applied researchers.</p></div></div></section>
<section class="section research-selector" id="research" data-research-selector data-research-default="research-complex-treatments" data-research-placement="end"><div class="wrap"><div class="section-heading"><div><h2>Research areas</h2></div></div><div class="research-grid"><a class="research-choice" href="#research-complex-treatments" data-research-select aria-controls="research-complex-treatments">Complex treatments</a><a class="research-choice" href="#research-targeted-learning" data-research-select aria-controls="research-targeted-learning">Targeted learning</a><a class="research-choice" href="#research-conformal-inference" data-research-select aria-controls="research-conformal-inference">Conformal inference</a><a class="research-choice" href="#research-population-health" data-research-select aria-controls="research-population-health">Population health</a><div class="research-panels" data-research-panels><article class="research-area-detail" id="research-complex-treatments" data-research-panel role="region" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="research-complex-treatments-title"><div class="research-visual"><img src="assets/line-complex.svg?v=6" alt="" width="300" height="150" loading="lazy"></div><div class="research-area-copy"><h3 id="research-complex-treatments-title">Causal estimation with complex exposures</h3><div class="research-area-body"><p>Methods for estimating causal effects of treatments with multiple levels or complex exposures within the potential outcomes framework. We combine doubly robust estimation, cross-fitting and influence-function-based inference, including when nuisance models are estimated with machine learning. The <a href="#software">Software</a> section includes the <code>tmleMulti</code> implementation.</p></div></div></article><article class="research-area-detail" id="research-targeted-learning" data-research-panel role="region" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="research-targeted-learning-title"><div class="research-visual"><img src="assets/line-targeted.svg?v=15" alt="" width="300" height="150" loading="lazy"></div><div class="research-area-copy"><h3 id="research-targeted-learning-title">Targeted learning &amp; semiparametric efficiency</h3><div class="research-area-body"><p>Methods that combine statistical learning with causal estimation, including targeted maximum likelihood estimation (TMLE) and doubly robust approaches. Semiparametric efficiency theory, influence functions and the delta method provide a basis for inference and variance estimation.</p></div></div></article><article class="research-area-detail" id="research-conformal-inference" data-research-panel role="region" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="research-conformal-inference-title"><div class="research-visual"><img src="assets/line-conformal.svg?v=13" alt="" width="300" height="150" loading="lazy"></div><div class="research-area-copy"><h3 id="research-conformal-inference-title">Conformal inference for causal questions</h3><div class="research-area-body"><p>Conformal methods for quantifying uncertainty in causal estimands, including settings that use machine learning or have small samples. We investigate the assumptions and conditions under which finite-sample coverage can be guaranteed.</p></div></div></article><article class="research-area-detail" id="research-population-health" data-research-panel role="region" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="research-population-health-title"><div class="research-visual"><img src="assets/line-population.svg?v=5" alt="" width="300" height="150" loading="lazy"></div><div class="research-area-copy"><h3 id="research-population-health-title">Computational epidemiology &amp; inequalities in cancer</h3><div class="research-area-body"><p>Applications of causal inference and computational epidemiology to population health. Topics include socioeconomic inequalities in cancer outcomes, emergency presentation and cancer survival, and reproducible, data-adaptive estimation.</p></div></div></article></div></div></div><svg class="home-wave" viewBox="0 0 1440 80" preserveAspectRatio="none" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"><path d="M0 16 C280 16 420 32 700 48 C980 64 1170 64 1440 64 L1440 80 H0 Z"/></svg></section>
